text:
The scoreboard says 6-2 and the chances say this was close to even. Both are true, and the gap between them has a name: Lukas Dostal. Anaheim's goalie allowed six goals on 25 shots, 3.7 more than those shots usually produce, and Simon Holmstrom took three of them on three shots.

The tone was set early and strangely. Ben Hutton scored 1:55 in on a shot that goes in about 1% of the time. Bo Horvat made it 2-0 on a power play early in the second, and when Nikita Nesterenko got one back 62 seconds later, Holmstrom answered 26 seconds after that. He scored again at 8:28, Mitchell Chaffee made it 5-1 two minutes later, and the game was gone inside half a period. Cutter Gauthier tipped one in late in the second to keep his goal streak going, and Holmstrom finished the hat trick 2:41 into the third.

The odd part is that Anaheim owned the second period on chances, 1.70 expected goals to 1.14, and led shot attempts 60-46 for the night. The Ducks won this game in 54% of our replays of every shot. Alex Killorn had the best look of the night, a 44% chance in the second, and missed the net. Semyon Varlamov stopped 26 of 28 for his first regulation win since coming back from injury, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner.

Matthew Schaefer had three assists in nearly 26 minutes and blocked what would have been a tap-in, two days after his 100th NHL game. The Islanders finished their California trip 2-0-1, with Mathew Barzal back in the lineup, but lost Logan Stanley to a lower-body injury, and Horvat did not play the final 4:17, which is worth watching. Anaheim turns around and hosts Calgary tonight.
headline: Holmstrom's hat trick turns an even game into a rout
